channel.title: US Visa Policy (English)
channel.description: USCIS and State Department policy updates in five languages

item.title: DHS Proposes $70,000 Initial and $30,000 Subsequent Fees for F-1 OPT
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security has filed a proposed rule that would create new fees for Optional Practical Training (OPT) under the F-1 student visa program. The rule would require a $70,000 fee for initial OPT and a $30,000 fee for any subsequent OPT period, applying to each F-1 student at a SEVP-certified institution.

item.title: Italian National Indicted for Voting in 2024 Election and Lying on Naturalization Form
item.description: USCIS assisted in the federal investigation leading to the indictment of Andrea Catanese, a 60-year-old Italian national, for voting while not a U.S. citizen and making false statements on his naturalization application. If convicted on all counts, he faces up to 10 years in federal prison.

item.title: DHS Waives Certain Laws to Speed Border Wall Construction in New Mexico
item.description: The Secretary of Homeland Security has determined, under section 102 of IIRIRA, that certain federal and state legal requirements will be waived to allow expedited construction of border barriers and roads in a segment of New Mexico within the El Paso Sector. The determination took effect on October 2, 2026.

item.title: Former Syrian Prison Warden Sentenced to 60 Years for Torture and Immigration Fraud
item.description: Samir Ousman Alsheikh, a former warden of Syria's Adra Prison and provincial governor, was sentenced to 60 years in prison for torture and immigration fraud. USCIS assisted in the investigation that led to his conviction.

item.title: White House Sets FY2027 Refugee Ceiling at 17,500, Prioritizes South African Afrikaners
item.description: On September 25, 2026, the President issued Presidential Determination No. 2026-24, setting the Fiscal Year 2027 refugee admissions ceiling at up to 17,500 and directing that admissions be primarily allocated to Afrikaners from South Africa under Executive Order 14204. The determination was published in the Federal Register on October 2, 2026.

item.title: Federal Grand Jury Indicts Ten Noncitizens for Voter Fraud in Minnesota
item.description: On Sept. 24, a federal grand jury separately indicted ten noncitizens for voter fraud in Minnesota elections. The investigation was led by ICE Homeland Security Investigations with assistance from USCIS. All defendants have made their initial court appearances.

item.title: DHS Raises Two HR-1 Immigration Enforcement Fees to $5,300 for FY2027
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security has issued its fiscal year 2027 inflation adjustment for two immigration enforcement fees created by HR-1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Both fees, which apply to aliens arrested after an in absentia removal order and to inadmissible aliens apprehended between ports of entry, rise from $5,130 to $5,300. DHS will begin assessing and collecting the new amounts on October 16, 2026.

item.title: DHS Sets FY 2027 Inflation Adjustments for Parole, I-94, ESTA and EVUS Fees
item.description: DHS has announced Fiscal Year 2027 inflation-adjusted amounts for certain immigration fees required by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (HR-1), including the parole fee, ESTA fee and EVUS enrollment fee. The new amounts take effect October 16, 2026. The Form I-94 fee at land border ports of entry will not change for FY 2027 due to the statutory rounding rule.

item.title: USCIS Announces FY2027 Inflation Adjustment to H.R. 1 Immigration Fees
item.description: USCIS has published the Fiscal Year 2027 inflation adjustment to immigration fees established under H.R. 1 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act). The adjustment reflects a 3.36 percent increase in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) between July 2025 and July 2026. The new fees take effect for requests postmarked on or after October 16, 2026.

item.title: USCIS Finalizes EB-5 Fee Increases, Effective November 30, 2026
item.description: DHS and USCIS published a final rule adjusting fees for the EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program, codifying provisions of the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022. The rule takes effect November 30, 2026, and raises several Integrity Fund fees along with other EB-5 immigration benefit request fees. It responds to public comments on a proposed version of the rule published October 23, 2025.

item.title: USCIS Announces FY 2027 Inflation Adjustment for Certain H.R. 1 Immigration Fees
item.description: USCIS has published a Federal Register notice raising certain H.R. 1 immigration-related fees for fiscal year 2027 to account for inflation from July 2025 through July 2026. The new fees take effect on Oct. 16, 2026, and apply to requests postmarked on or after that date.

item.title: EOIR Announces FY2027 Inflation Adjustment to OBBBA Fees for Certain DHS Forms
item.description: The Department of Justice's Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) has issued a notice detailing FY2027 inflation adjustments to OBBBA fees for certain DHS forms filed in immigration court and before the Board of Immigration Appeals. The adjustments implement a final rule already published on August 21, 2026, and take effect October 1, 2026.

item.title: USCIS Helps Florida Charge 16 Noncitizens With Unlawful Voting
item.description: USCIS assisted a Florida investigation that led to charges against 16 noncitizens accused of registering to vote by falsely claiming U.S. citizenship and then voting. Four additional individuals were charged with voting while on felony probation. USCIS confirmed the alien status of the individuals involved, according to the Florida Attorney General's Office.

item.title: USCIS to Adjust EB-5 Fees to Cover Program Costs and Boost Integrity Measures
item.description: USCIS announced it is updating fees for the EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program so that fees fully recover the cost of running the program, meet statutory processing time goals, and support integrity measures such as audits and site visits. The change finalizes a proposed rule published by DHS in October 2025. The source does not specify exact new fee amounts.

item.title: Cuban National Convicted in International Alien Smuggling and Money Laundering Case
item.description: USCIS supported an investigation that led to the conviction of Lazaro Alain Cabrera-Rodriguez, a Cuban national, for conspiring to run an international alien smuggling organization and launder its proceeds. The organization charged between $1,500 and $40,000 per smuggled migrant and used fraudulent ESTA applications and false claims of European citizenship.

item.title: Romanian National Pleads Guilty to Conspiring in Marriage Fraud Scheme
item.description: Antonia-Beatrice Mircea, a Romanian citizen, admitted to conspiring with a U.S. citizen to enter a sham marriage to obtain lawful permanent residence. USCIS assisted the federal investigation, announced by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of New Jersey.

item.title: Two Aliens Charged in New Jersey With Illegal Voting and False Statements on N-400
item.description: USCIS assisted an investigation that led to charges against a Jamaican national and a Venezuelan national living in New Jersey, accused of voting in federal elections while not U.S. citizens and lying about it on their naturalization applications. Both allegedly certified falsely on voter registration forms that they were citizens and later denied voting history on Form N-400.

item.title: Nigerian National Indicted for Falsely Claiming Citizenship to Vote
item.description: A federal grand jury in Kansas indicted George Olawunmi Johnson, a Nigerian national and lawful permanent resident, for falsely claiming U.S. citizenship to register and vote in elections. USCIS assisted Homeland Security Investigations in the case.

item.title: Trump Proclamation Extends $100,000 H-1B Entry Restriction Through September 2027
item.description: Proclamation 11069, signed September 18, 2026, extends the 2025 H-1B entry restriction under Proclamation 10973 for an additional 12 months. H-1B specialty occupation workers outside the United States remain barred from entry unless their petition is accompanied by a $100,000 payment, except where DHS grants a national interest exception.

item.title: USCIS Reports Naturalization Fraud Charge and Three Denaturalization Cases in North Carolina
item.description: A federal grand jury in Charlotte indicted a naturalized citizen from Bhutan for naturalization fraud, alleging he concealed prior child sexual abuse when applying for citizenship. Separately, the U.S. Attorney's Office filed civil denaturalization complaints against three other individuals accused of obtaining citizenship through fraud or concealment of immigration violations.

item.title: Executive Order Strengthens Interagency Review of H-1B Visa Petitions
item.description: President Trump signed Executive Order 14431 on September 18, 2026, published in the Federal Register on September 23, 2026, directing closer coordination among federal agencies in reviewing H-1B petitions, labor condition applications and visas. The order responds to concerns about wage suppression, layoffs of American workers and outsourcing abuses linked to the H-1B program.

item.title: Haitian National Pleads Guilty to Illegally Voting in 2024 U.S. Election
item.description: A Haitian citizen, Valery Zidor, pleaded guilty in federal court in Miami to falsely claiming U.S. citizenship on voter registration forms and voting in the 2024 general election. USCIS assisted Homeland Security Investigations in the case.

item.title: Two Chinese Nationals Indicted on Naturalization Fraud and Firearms Charges
item.description: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Missouri announced that two Chinese nationals turned themselves in on Sept. 17 after being indicted on naturalization and firearms related charges. USCIS assisted in the investigation alongside the FBI and the U.S. Air Force Office of Special Investigations.

item.title: DHS Extends 'Mass Influx of Aliens' Finding for Another 180 Days
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security has extended its Finding of Mass Influx of Aliens, first issued in January 2025, for an additional 180 days. The finding allows DHS to request assistance from state and local law enforcement in administering immigration laws and cites continued strain on border and detention resources.

item.title: State Department Updates FOIA Rules, Clarifies Requirements for Visa Record Requests
item.description: The State Department has revised its public access to information regulations at 22 CFR Part 171 to reflect changes in agency organization and procedures, including electronic submission of requests. The rule updates how requesters should describe records sought and consolidates identity verification requirements. It takes effect on October 21, 2026.

item.title: DHS Issues Correction Restoring Evidence Rules for Children of Foreign Government Employees
item.description: DHS has issued a correcting amendment to the September 9, 2026 interim final rule (IFR) that allows children born in the United States to foreign government employees, who are not U.S. citizens, to register for lawful permanent residence. The correction restores evidentiary requirements that were inadvertently deleted in the original IFR and is applied retroactively to September 4, 2026.

item.title: State Department Delegates Visa Bond Waiver Authority to Senior Consular Officials
item.description: The State Department issued a notice delegating its authority to waive visa bond requirements under 22 CFR 41.11(c)(3) to the Principal Deputy Assistant Secretary and the Deputy Assistant Secretary for Visa Services. This is an internal administrative change specifying who may authorize such waivers on behalf of the Assistant Secretary for Consular Affairs.

item.title: DHS proposes to eliminate 60-day discretionary grace period for nonimmigrant workers
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security has proposed removing the regulation that currently allows up to a 60-day discretionary grace period for certain nonimmigrant workers and their dependents when their employment ends before their authorized stay expires. The change is only a proposal, not final, and public comments are accepted through November 10, 2026.

item.title: USCIS Announces H-2B Cap Reached for First Half of FY 2027
item.description: USCIS has received enough petitions to meet the congressionally mandated H-2B cap for the first half of fiscal year 2027. September 4, 2026 was the final receipt date for new cap-subject H-2B petitions requesting an employment start date before April 1, 2027. Petitions received after that date requesting such start dates will be rejected.

item.title: DHS Corrects Statistical Table in Proposed H-1B Fee Rule
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security issued a correction to Table 13 in its proposed rule on fees for certain H-1B petitions, originally published August 25, 2026. The correction fixes Form I-129 H-1B receipt statistics for fiscal years 2021 through 2025 and does not change the proposed fee itself.

item.title: Labor Day 2026 Proclamation Mentions Proposed New H-1B Visa Fee
item.description: The White House issued a presidential proclamation declaring September 7, 2026, as Labor Day. The proclamation briefly mentions a proposal for a new fee on H-1B visa petitions intended to encourage companies to hire American workers first.

item.title: State Department Designates Los Tiguerones as a Foreign Terrorist Organization
item.description: The U.S. Department of State has designated the group Los Tiguerones, also known as Los Fenix and Los Igualitos, as a Foreign Terrorist Organization under section 219 of the INA. The designation took effect upon publication in the Federal Register on September 10, 2026.

item.title: Federal Court Temporarily Halts USCIS Diversity Visa Hold Policy PM-602-0193
item.description: On Aug. 28, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California ordered a temporary vacatur of USCIS policy memorandum PM-602-0193, which had imposed a hold on certain Diversity Visa (DV) adjustment of status cases. USCIS must resume ordinary adjudication of affected applicants' cases for the remainder of the DV fiscal year while litigation continues.

item.title: DHS Issues Rule Allowing Certain Children of Foreign Government Employees to Register as LPRs
item.description: DHS has issued an interim final rule expanding eligibility for lawful permanent resident registration to certain children born in the United States to foreign government employees, not just foreign diplomatic officers. The rule implements Executive Order 14418 and takes effect September 4, 2026.

item.title: USCIS to Open New International Field Office in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
item.description: USCIS is opening a new international field office in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, beginning operations on September 9, 2026. The office will directly handle document verification, fraud investigations, and DNA collection for family relationship confirmation, functions previously coordinated with the Department of State.

item.title: DHS Corrects Cost-Benefit Table in Rule on Asylum Referrals Without Interview
item.description: DHS published a correction to a cost-and-benefit table (Table 3) in its rule on Affirmative Asylum Referrals Without Interview, originally issued July 28, 2026. The correction fixes formatting in the table and does not change the substance of the rule.

item.title: Court Enjoins USCIS Hold Policies, Certifies Class in Red Eagle Law v. Edlow
item.description: On Aug. 24, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California enjoined USCIS Policy Memoranda PM-602-0192 and PM-602-0194, which had placed adjudication holds on certain applications. The court also certified a class of affected applicants and ordered USCIS to resume normal processing of their cases.

item.title: CBP Establishes Four Customs-Enforcement Areas to Combat Maritime Smuggling
item.description: U.S. Customs and Border Protection has declared four Customs-Enforcement Areas (CEAs) in the near shore waters of South Florida, Central/Southern California, Puerto Rico, and the Gulf Coast of Texas. The declaration extends CBP's enforcement authority from 12 nautical miles to 24 nautical miles from the baseline to target hovering vessels used for smuggling people and goods.

item.title: DHS Proposes New $103,265 Fee for H-1B Cap-Subject Petitions
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security has proposed a new $103,265 fee for all H-1B cap-subject petitions, including those eligible for the advanced degree exemption. The fee would be payable by the petitioner at the time of filing and would come on top of all other applicable fees or payments. This is a proposed rule, not yet final, with a public comment period closing September 24, 2026.

item.title: USCIS to Issue New Form I-485 Edition, Rejecting Older Versions From Sept. 18
item.description: USCIS will publish a revised edition of Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status, dated 09/18/26, effective Sept. 18, 2026. The revision aligns the form with the recently announced Public Charge Ground of Inadmissibility Final Rule, and there is no grace period between editions.
